string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of its four direct-administered municipalities. Located in the north of the country, it serves as the political, cultural, and educational centre of China. The city is home to world-famous historical sites, including the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, and the Temple of Heaven, which attract millions of visitors every year. Beijing also hosts the headquarters of many major Chinese state-owned companies and government institutions. In recent decades it has developed into a modern global city while preserving its rich cultural heritage. It hosted the 2008 Summer Olympic Games and, together with Zhangjiakou, the 2022 Winter Olympic Games.

Shanghai is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities and the country\'s largest city by population. Situated at the mouth of the Yangtze River on the eastern coast, it has long been China\'s most important commercial and financial centre. The city is known for its iconic skyline along the Huangpu River, featuring landmarks such as the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Shanghai Tower. Its historic waterfront district, the Bund, displays a collection of colonial-era architecture. Shanghai is home to the Shanghai Stock Exchange and hosts the headquarters of many international banks and companies. It is also a major port and a hub for trade, innovation, and international business in East Asia.

Chongqing is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities, located in the southwestern part of the country. It is one of the largest cities in the world by population and administrative area. Known as the Mountain City, Chongqing is built on rugged hills where the Jialing River meets the Yangtze River, creating dramatic views of layered streets and bridges. The city served as the temporary capital of China during the Second World War and played an important role in modern Chinese history. Today it is a major industrial, transport, and logistics hub, with a growing high-technology sector. Its famous hotpot cuisine and night-time cityscape make it a popular destination for domestic tourists.

Tianjin is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities, located in the northern part of the country along the coast of the Bohai Sea. It is an important port city and industrial centre that serves as the gateway to Beijing, which lies about 120 kilometres to the northwest. Tianjin has a distinctive blend of Chinese and European influences, reflected in its many colonial-era buildings, particularly in the historic Five Great Avenues area. The city played a significant role in China\'s modernisation during the late Qing dynasty and was one of the first treaty ports to open to foreign trade. Today, Tianjin is known for its strong manufacturing base, its port, and its rapidly developing economic zones.
